mentl/9840121:
Recursive nested fns like `fn go(i, acc) = ... go(...) ...` capture their own
name in the closure. The closure-construction emit stored `(local.get $go)
(i32.store offset=12)` BEFORE the LLet's `(local.set $go)` fired — so the
self-ref slot stored uninitialized $go (= 0). At runtime, `go(...)` recursive
call read fn_idx=0 from offset 0, dispatched to funcref[0] (typically a
unary fn), and trapped with `indirect call type mismatch`.

Substrate truth (per protocol_handler_is_state_is_closure_is_evidence.md):
the fn IS the closure record IS __state at runtime. The recursive
self-reference is the closure-being-constructed. $state_tmp at cap-store
time holds exactly that pointer.

Fix: emit_llet detects when value is LMakeClosure (tag 311) and routes to
$emit_lmakeclosure_into_local, which assigns the local IMMEDIATELY after
alloc. Subsequent `(local.get $<name>)` for self-ref captures then reads
the closure record under construction. Non-self-ref captures unchanged
(they read other locals that were already assigned).

Empirical:
- Pre-fix: m2 traps `indirect call type mismatch` at parse_int_go on any
  input.
- Post-fix: m2 compiles `fn main() = 42` cleanly; m2 also compiles the
  full wheel end-to-end (m3 = 1141 bytes, exit 0, zero stderr). L1
  pipeline structurally unblocked. Fixpoint not yet reached
  (m2.wat=4.1MB vs m3.wat=1141 bytes — wheel-emit cascade
  Hβ.first-light.wheel-emit-implementation #111 still has many gaps),
  but the seed→wheel→m3 round-trip now runs.

tokensafe/98b409d:
API keys let power users skip x402 per-request payments in exchange for
a subscription. Keys use X-API-Key header (not Bearer, to avoid conflict
with webhook admin auth). SHA-256 hashed in SQLite — full key shown once
on creation.

Two tiers: Pro ($49/mo, 6K checks/month, 200 req/min) and Enterprise
($199/mo, unlimited, 600 req/min). Middleware runs before x402 gate —
valid key present means x402 settlement is skipped entirely. Per-key
rate limiter is independent of per-IP limiter.

CRUD routes (POST/GET/DELETE /v1/api-keys, GET /v1/api-keys/:id/usage)
reuse existing webhookAuth bearer middleware. Usage tracked per key per
calendar month (UTC) via upsert. Response headers expose tier, usage
count, and reset date.

304 tests across 9 files (34 new: 18 unit + 16 integration).
perennials/984163a:
The sun's bed-shade lines read keptPlants to count how many of her kept
plants suit each bed's light, but keptPlants was declared lower in the
component than the lines that used it. A yard with a drawn bed therefore
threw a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError the moment the model view asked
for the shade, taking the whole page down; a yard with no bed never touched
the binding and looked fine, which is why it slipped the first drive. The
kept list is resolved once now, right after the dataset is in hand and well
above every reader, and the model raises over a bedded yard.

perennials/9808a5c:
The Share export carried the plan and stopped there, so the handout showed
where everything goes and nothing of what it grows into, which is half of
what a planting plan is for. When any placed plant has a height, the
elevation now joins the exported sheet below the plan: ground line, height
rule, the earth wash, and every figure standing as she saw it, with the
stand line printed in the footer beside the bloom line. A yard of bare
marks adds no band, because it would say nothing the plan doesn't.

The figures come from one geometry. figurePaths in lib/elevation.ts now
owns the archetype drawing, ElevationView renders it and the export prints
it, so the figure a client is handed is the figure she saw, and a shape
tweak lands in both places or neither. rules.test.ts pins that every
archetype draws, that only the tree layers carry trunks, and that only
the root layer reaches below the line.

The footer stops being a fixed-height slab: it lays out whatever coverage
lines the sheet earned and the raster sizes to fit.
